title: The seven groups
intro: Scientists sort insects into orders by their wings, their mouths and how they grow. Let's meet seven groups, starting with the most colorful ones.

lessons.title: Lepidoptera: butterflies and moths
lessons.intro: Lepidoptera means “scaly wings”. They are butterflies and moths.
lessons.closing: Butterflies and moths pollinate flowers and are food for birds. Their caterpillars eat leaves, but the plant almost always recovers.

exercises.prompt: What covers a butterfly's wings?
exercises.explanation: Lepidoptera means “scaly wing”: thousands of colored scales.

exercises.prompt: What is an adult butterfly's mouth like?
options: A coiled tube for sipping nectar
exercises.explanation: Its tube uncoils like a straw to drink nectar.

exercises.prompt: Match each one with what makes it special.

pairs.right: Antennae with a little knob at the tip

exercises.explanation: Looking at the antennae tells butterflies from moths.

exercises.prompt: Put the butterfly's life cycle in order.
exercises.explanation: Lepidoptera go through complete metamorphosis.

exercises.prompt: How are butterflies useful?
options: They pollinate flowers and feed birds
exercises.explanation: They carry pollen from flower to flower and feed other animals.

lessons.title: Coleoptera: beetles
lessons.intro: Coleoptera means “sheathed wings”. It's the biggest group of animals in the world: beetles, ladybugs and fireflies.
lessons.closing: Beetles recycle leaves and wood, and some, like the ladybug, eat pests. There are more kinds of beetles than of any other animal!

exercises.prompt: What are a beetle's front wings like?
options: Hard like a case: the elytra
exercises.explanation: The elytra protect the thin wings it flies with.

exercises.prompt: Tap all the beetles (Coleoptera).
exercises.explanation: Ladybug, firefly and beetle have elytra: they're beetles.

exercises.prompt: What is a beetle's mouth like?
options: For chewing: it bites and chews
exercises.explanation: Its jaws chew leaves, wood or small prey.

exercises.prompt: Which group of animals has the most species in the world?
exercises.explanation: There are more beetle species than any other group of animals.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence.
exercises.sentence: Beetles ___ leaves, wood and leftovers, and that feeds the soil.
exercises.explanation: They are nature's recyclers.

lessons.title: Hymenoptera: bees, wasps and ants
lessons.intro: Hymenoptera means “membrane wings”, that is, thin see-through wings. They are bees, wasps and ants. Many live in groups and share the work.
lessons.closing: Bees pollinate many of the fruits we eat. They only sting to defend themselves: if you stay calm, they go on their way.

exercises.prompt: How many pairs of wings does a bee have?
exercises.explanation: Two pairs of thin wings, like membranes.

exercises.prompt: Tap all the Hymenoptera.
exercises.explanation: Bees and ants are Hymenoptera. Ants are cousins of bees!

exercises.prompt: Why does a bee sting?
options: To defend itself or its hive
exercises.explanation: It only stings if it feels attacked.

exercises.prompt: What do bees do that helps us have fruit?
exercises.explanation: By carrying pollen between flowers, flowers turn into fruit.

exercises.prompt: If a bee flies near you, what's best to do?
exercises.explanation: Sudden moves scare it. If you stay calm, it will go on its way.

lessons.title: Odonata: dragonflies
lessons.intro: Odonata comes from “tooth”: they have strong mouths to catch prey. They are dragonflies and damselflies.
lessons.closing: Dragonflies eat loads of mosquitoes and usually live where the water is clean. If you see lots of dragonflies, it's usually a good sign!

exercises.prompt: What are a dragonfly's wings like?
options: Long, narrow and see-through, with veins like a net
exercises.explanation: Four long wings it moves separately: that's why it flies so well!

exercises.prompt: What do dragonflies eat?
exercises.explanation: They are hunters: they catch mosquitoes in the air.

exercises.prompt: If there are lots of dragonflies at a river, what does it tell us?
options: That the water is usually clean
exercises.explanation: Lots of dragonflies is usually a good sign: their nymphs need clean water to grow.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence.
exercises.explanation: Their nymphs grow underwater and then fly away.

exercises.prompt: Do dragonflies sting people?
exercises.explanation: They don't sting people: they're harmless and eat mosquitoes.

lessons.title: Orthoptera: grasshoppers and crickets
lessons.intro: Orthoptera means “straight wings”. They are grasshoppers and crickets, like our friend Paquito. They have big back legs for jumping.
lessons.closing: Grasshoppers and crickets are food for birds, frogs and lizards. Only some locusts become pests, when there are huge numbers of them.

exercises.prompt: Why are their back legs so big?
exercises.explanation: Their back legs work like springs.

exercises.prompt: What is their mouth like?
exercises.explanation: They have jaws to chew plants.

exercises.prompt: Match each one with what makes it special.
exercises.explanation: Grasshoppers, crickets and locusts are cousins.

exercises.prompt: How do grasshoppers grow?
options: With incomplete metamorphosis: egg, nymph and adult
With a caterpillar and a chrysalis
exercises.explanation: The nymph looks like the adult and grows by molting.

exercises.prompt: Who eats grasshoppers?
exercises.explanation: They are an important part of the food chain.

lessons.title: Hemiptera: true bugs and cicadas
lessons.intro: Hemiptera means “half wing”, because in true bugs the front wings are half hard and half thin. They are true bugs, cicadas and aphids, and they all have a needle-like mouth.
lessons.closing: Many bugs are harmless and some eat other pests. We look at them calmly without touching: that way we don't bother them and they don't bother us.

exercises.prompt: What is a stink bug's mouth like?
options: Like a needle to pierce and suck
exercises.explanation: It pierces plants and sucks their juice.

exercises.prompt: What do many stink bugs do to defend themselves?
options: They give off a strong smell
exercises.explanation: That's why some are called “stink bugs”.

exercises.prompt: Tap the Hemiptera.
exercises.explanation: The stink bug has half-hard, half-thin wings and a needle mouth.

exercises.prompt: What is a cicada?
options: A Hemiptera that sings very loudly on hot days
exercises.explanation: The male cicada sings by vibrating membranes on its body.

exercises.prompt: If you see a stink bug, what do you do?
options: I look at it without touching
I grab it with my hand
exercises.explanation: Look without touching: that way neither of you bothers the other.

lessons.title: Diptera: flies and mosquitoes
lessons.intro: Diptera means “two wings”. Flies and mosquitoes have only one pair of wings. They have a bad reputation, but they do very important jobs.
lessons.closing: Flies recycle leftovers and many pollinate flowers. Some mosquitoes spread disease: that's why we protect ourselves from their bites.

exercises.prompt: How many pairs of wings does a fly have?
exercises.explanation: Just one pair: that's why they're called Diptera, “two wings”.

exercises.prompt: What important job do many flies do?
options: They break down leftovers and clean up nature
exercises.explanation: Without flies, leftovers would take much longer to disappear.

exercises.prompt: Tap all the Diptera.
exercises.explanation: Flies and mosquitoes have just one pair of wings.

exercises.prompt: What are fly larvae like?
exercises.explanation: Diptera larvae have no legs.

exercises.prompt: Put each insect in its group.
exercises.explanation: Scaly wings, case wings, membrane wings and just one pair of wings.

exam.title: Unit challenge
exam.intro: The seven groups challenge! Ten questions to see if you can tell them apart. Pass it and you open the last unit.
exam.closing: Now you know the seven groups! Look at their wings and mouths and you'll know which group each insect belongs to.

exercises.prompt: What does “Lepidoptera” mean?
exercises.explanation: Butterflies and moths: scaly wings.

exercises.prompt: Which group has hard front wings like a case?
exercises.explanation: Coleoptera: beetles, ladybugs and fireflies.

exercises.prompt: Match each group with its examples.
exercises.explanation: Four groups, four kinds of wings.

exercises.prompt: How many pairs of wings do Diptera have?
exercises.explanation: Only one pair: instead of a second pair they have two little knobs that help them keep their balance when flying.

exercises.prompt: Put each insect in its group.
exercises.explanation: A caterpillar is a young butterfly: it's Lepidoptera too.

exercises.prompt: If there are lots of dragonflies at a river, what does it tell us?
options: That the water is usually clean
exercises.explanation: Their nymphs grow in the water and need it clean: lots of dragonflies is usually a good sign.

exercises.prompt: Why does a bee sting?
options: To defend itself or its hive
exercises.explanation: To defend itself.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence.
exercises.sentence: Stink bugs defend themselves by giving off a strong ___.
exercises.explanation: A strong smell.

exercises.prompt: What is an adult butterfly's mouth like?
options: A coiled tube for sipping nectar
exercises.explanation: A tube for sipping nectar.

exercises.prompt: Tap all the beetles (Coleoptera).
exercises.explanation: The ones with elytra.
